The two peaks are the in-phase and out-of-phase combinations of the two well states. They are at about 86.8 meV and 141.4 meV, so the splitting is about 55 meV.

**Method.** The structure is symmetric about the centre of the middle barrier, so I treated the even and odd half-structures separately.

1. With ħ²/2m* = 0.0380998/0.067 = 0.5687 eV nm², the wavevectors are k = √(E/0.5687) in the wells and contacts, and κ = √((0.30−E)/0.5687) in the barriers.
2. Start at the centre of the middle barrier with ψ = cosh κx (even) or sinh κx (odd). Propagate through the half barrier (0.75 nm), the 4 nm well, and the outer 1.5 nm barrier. At the outer edge this gives a log-derivative Λ_e or Λ_o.
3. Matching to the outgoing contact wave gives T = sin²[arctan(Λ_e/k) − arctan(Λ_o/k)]. A peak (T = 1) occurs when this phase difference Δ equals −π/2 modulo π.
4. I evaluated Δ(E) by hand at several energies:

| E (eV) | Δ (rad) |
|---|---|
| 0.080 | −0.81 |
| 0.087 | −1.589 |
| 0.090 | −1.875 |
| 0.100 | −2.11 |
| 0.120 | −2.29 |
| 0.140 | −1.633 |
| 0.145 | −1.398 |

5. Interpolating to Δ = −π/2 gives the two peaks: E₁ ≈ 86.8 meV and E₂ ≈ 141.4 meV.

The hand arithmetic limits the precision to roughly ±0.3 meV.

Splitting ≈ 141.4 − 86.8 ≈ 54.6 meV.

ANSWER: {"splitting_meV": 54.6}
